analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 to 0.5012, versus the supplied parent reference of 0.5125 and historical best of 0.5312 (drops of 0.0113 and 0.0300). Per-category HR@10 was 0.515 for Movies_and_TV, 0.585 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.425 for Electronics, and 0.480 for CDs_and_Vinyl. These results do not support adding causal channel gates in this configuration. They do not establish why performance declined or isolate effects by category without parent category scores. The gates initially multiply first-convolution features by sigmoid(2), approximately 0.881, so initialization also changes feature scale. Allocated GPU time was 753.63 seconds. No test results were provided.
code_summary: One independently trained ConvRec checkpoint per category, with strict loading and four-category routing. Each network uses 96-dimensional item embeddings, eight causal residual convolution blocks with dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8], two-head causal attention with learned relative-distance bias, and a jointly trained gated prefix-history projection. The experimental change adds a causal three-tap channel gate to each residual block, multiplying GELU first-convolution outputs by sigmoid gate outputs; gate weights start at zero and biases at 2. Training retains 512 sampled negatives, uniform per-history cross-entropy reduction, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, seed 42, and validation checkpoint selection. Checks cover finite gate gradients, causality, zero padded outputs, and prediction parity after strict reload. The predictor reconstructs the same architecture and uses exactly one selected checkpoint per category, without ensembling.
